wstep: This card describes NCHFP pickled bell peppers in a vinegar, sugar and water brine, filled into sterile jars and processed in a boiling-water bath. [T:ACI-202,ACI-204,ACI-205]

sekcje.naglowek: Why the recipe must not be changed
akapity: The whole product needs a minimum, uniform level of acid to prevent the growth of botulism bacteria. [T:ACI-017]
Do not change the proportions of vinegar, vegetables and water, and do not use vinegar of unknown acidity; use only recipes with tested proportions. [T:ACI-016]
For pickles, white distilled vinegar and cider vinegar with 5% acidity are recommended. [T:ACI-018]
Penn State Extension advises vinegar of 5–7% acidity for home food preservation and advises against diluting vinegar with water unless a research-tested recipe says so. [T:ACI-209,ACI-210]

JarAtlas rule (cautious, for readers outside the USA): use white distilled (spirit) vinegar or cider vinegar labelled 5% or 6% acidity; do not use 10% vinegar and do not dilute it with water to make 5% vinegar; add only the water the recipe lists. [T:ACI-211,ACI-018]
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml. [T:ACI-195]

For about 9 pint jars NCHFP uses 7 pounds (about 3.2 kg) of firm bell peppers, 3 1/2 cups of sugar, 3 cups of vinegar with 5% acidity, 3 cups of water, 9 cloves of garlic and 4 1/2 teaspoons of canning or pickling salt. [T:ACI-202]

NCHFP puts the empty jars right side up on the rack in a boiling-water canner and fills the canner and jars with hot (not boiling) water to 1 inch (about 2.5 cm) above the tops of the jars. [T:SLO-120]
To sterilize empty jars, NCHFP boils them for 10 minutes below 1000 ft, and above that 1 minute longer for each additional thousand feet. [T:SLO-118]
JarAtlas rule for metres: boil the jars for 10 minutes up to 300 m, and add 1 minute for every further 300 m or part of it. [T:SLO-119]
Wash the peppers, cut them into quarters, remove the cores and seeds, cut away any blemishes and slice the peppers into strips. [T:ACI-203]
Boil the sugar, vinegar and water for 1 minute, add the peppers and bring to a boil. [T:ACI-203]
Remove and drain the hot sterilized jars one at a time, just before filling them. [T:SLO-120]
Put 1/2 clove of garlic and 1/4 teaspoon of salt in each sterile half-pint jar, and double the amounts for pint jars. [T:ACI-204]
Add the pepper strips and cover them with the hot vinegar mixture, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace. [T:ACI-204]
Put on the lids and process. [T:ACI-204]
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process half-pint and pint jars in a boiling-water bath for 5 minutes. [T:ACI-205,ACI-176]
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased. [T:ACI-015]
At 1001–6000 ft (above 300 m up to 1800 m) process half-pints and pints for 10 minutes. [T:ACI-206,ACI-176]
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process half-pints and pints for 15 minutes. [T:ACI-207,ACI-176]
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m. [T:ACI-176]
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage. [T:ACI-015]
The NCHFP table gives times only for half-pint and pint jars. [T:ACI-208]
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): a pint holds about 473 ml, so a 0.5 l jar has no tested time in this recipe; use jars of up to 473 ml. [T:ACI-179,ACI-174]
